chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Ma'bad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abu Khidash from Ali ibn Isma'il from Muhammad ibn 'Abdah al-Naysaburi who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is the cup of Nabidh and the cup of wine equal?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, equal.' I said, 'So the legal penalty (Hadd) in both of them is equal?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Equal.'

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Nabidh, a fermented drink made from raisins or barley
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: Hadd, the fixed legal penalty for a specific crime

ai.seo_question: What is the legal penalty for drinking Nabidh compared to wine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the distinction between Nabidh (fermented drink) and wine lies in the degree of intoxication rather than the substance itself, establishing that the legal penalty (Hadd) applies equally once either becomes intoxicating. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'idraj al-khamr fi al-nabidh' (the inclusion of wine within Nabidh), emphasizing that the cause of prohibition is intoxication itself. The ruling underscores the consistency of divine law in treating the effect of the substance as the primary criterion for legal accountability.
